review_items.rationale:
Reviewed fixed artifact e4465cc7b4964f2faf0e4099ccd60176, its stored plan and harness, and raw stdout/stderr for c611aead474d4b8fa96906fb00bd1771 against claim version 1. The duty is preservation of the original SystemCtx for each remote read released by prefix confirmation, supported by the explicit per-prefix ctx/from test expectation and exact-context consumer. It is not a successful-completion deadline. Launch constructs three configured full voters and bootstrap entries. The driver applies only committed bootstrap membership and the empty leader entry; it never changes term, role, pending reads or generated message contents. Tick-driven election actually reaches term 2 and current-term commit 4; setup assertions check all nodes committed/applied at 4 and known leader 1. Storage Append/SetState precedes message exposure; Update Commit and NotifyRaftLastApplied retain caller completion order for this synchronous non-crashing history. A globally FIFO queue is a permitted restriction of per-route ordering and does not serialize the two pending reads: both are observed pending before confirmation. The two first-context heartbeats are dropped at send admission, a failure explicitly permitted by Transport.send and not retried by NodeHost.sendMessage; later traffic is generated by real Peer handlers and delivered without reordering. The known-peer Peer.Handle checks and current-term checks remain active. No background owners, sleeps, shutdown, forged replies or hidden callbacks participate.

Raw events 18 and 19 admit distinct requester identities 2 and 3, with queued=true, two pending requests, current-term commit, sampled index 4 and original contexts (1001,101)/(2001,202). Both actual nonzero-context heartbeat replies originate from voters in term 2. The first suffices with leader self-support to release the prefix. Raw result 24 for requester 2 contains one response context (2001,202), released=true, leader_pending=0 and queue_empty=true; its actual follower ReadyToRead also contains (2001,202) at index 4. Result 25 for requester 3 contains its correct (2001,202), also released=true. Thus both antecedents are observed true, not vacuous. The raw wire records independently exhibit the wrong leader-to-2 response. The monitor correlates each admitted operation by scenario/requester, not the compared context, and checks exact serialized complete High/Low context lists. Both sides use the same Go struct encoder; the observed lists each have one element, so the decisive mismatch is content identity, not cardinality or order. A comparison on response count alone would miss it. The run has no parser gaps and both admissions have results. The sent slice is an immutable copied message history accumulated by the sole goroutine; ReadyToRead values are copied before Peer.Commit clears the producer queue. Absence from pending is valid release evidence in this suffix because no reset/removal path runs and source confirm is the deletion owner.

The implementation cause agrees with the measurement: confirm retains original s.ctx and s.from while releasing the prefix, but the remote send loop uses m.Hint/m.HintHigh for each s.from; the local branch correctly uses s.ctx. The exact-key client consumer cannot associate this wrong context with requester 2 original batch. That final NodeHost timeout consequence is source-supported risk, not an executed endpoint result. No correspondence issue was found for this complete local counterexample.

Explained alternatives and bounded contrary observations: The later request succeeds in the same run: requester 3 receives its own (2001,202), so the finding is not a blanket failure of remote ReadIndex. The source local-completion branch uses s.ctx correctly; no local-prefix violation is claimed. Requester timeout/GC remains available and prevents inferring permanent resource retention. The test process passed because it emitted measurements for the monitor; process success is not the property verdict.

feedback.answered: Initial A1 source trace: leader append assigns current term/index, updates its own match, and replication responses update remote match; tryCommit selects voting-member quorum match and asks the log to commit only in the current term. Followers validate the preceding log term, append, and bound advertised commit by the matched suffix. Initial A2 trace: elections reset term/votes/progress and gather votes after log freshness checks; higher-term dispatch changes role and lower-term messages are dropped. Reset discards pending read confirmations and initializes follower progress, while leader promotion appends a current-term no-op. Election is suppressed when committed work has not yet applied, with a comment explicitly tying this to membership/quorum safety. These traces do not yet establish persistence ordering or application/membership completion. Early sourced discrepancy: readIndex.confirm releases a prefix of pending requests and retains each request ctx/from, but handleReadIndexLeaderConfirmation sends every remote response using the confirming message Hint/HintHigh, whereas local completion uses s.ctx. Followers copy the response context to ReadyToRead; pendingReadIndex.addReady selects a batch by exact SystemCtx. Thus a prefix request with a different context appears not to receive its own completion key. Timeout/GC exists and is contrary evidence against permanent resource retention; no execution or normative conclusion is claimed.

formation.explanation: Node batches proposals into Peer under raftMu. Leader stamps term/index, replicates to members and advances commitment from voting match order statistic only for its current term. Followers require preceding term match and protect the committed prefix, replying after engine persistence. Conflicts reduce next and retry; snapshots resynchronize missing history. Engine exposes committed entries to the RSM queue, whose application/session results and applied index drive client consumption. ReadIndex separately samples committed index, gathers heartbeat confirmation and releases pending prefixes to local readiness or remote responses.

context.explanation: Per-cluster term, role and applied membership define authority. Timers launch elections for eligible full members only after committed work is applied; votes require fresh log and no conflicting vote. Candidate quorum promotes and appends a current-term no-op. Higher terms demote/reset; lower terms are rejected. CheckQuorum may revoke leadership; transfer waits for target match and uses TimeoutNow, while proposals are dropped during transfer. Configuration application changes participant maps and local removal revokes leadership. Restart restores persisted term/vote/log but initializes transient follower context.

connection.explanation: Term dispatch precedes response consumption. Reset clears old votes, replication progress and pending ReadIndex support while retaining established log/commit; leader must form current-term commitment before multi-voter reads. Log freshness and committed-prefix protection constrain future leaders. Election waits for application so committed membership changes affect later quorums; RSM changes update Peer under raftMu. Old client work can be dropped or time out independently of preserved decisions. Read confirmation is transient; exact context and applied-index checks bridge its publication to requester completion, making remote prefix correlation a concrete unresolved consumption premise.

feedback.answered: Initial A1 source trace: leader append assigns current term/index, updates its own match, and replication responses update remote match; tryCommit selects voting-member quorum match and asks the log to commit only in the current term. Followers validate the preceding log term, append, and bound advertised commit by the matched suffix. Initial A2 trace: elections reset term/votes/progress and gather votes after log freshness checks; higher-term dispatch changes role and lower-term messages are dropped. Reset discards pending read confirmations and initializes follower progress, while leader promotion appends a current-term no-op. Election is suppressed when committed work has not yet applied, with a comment explicitly tying this to membership/quorum safety. These traces do not yet establish persistence ordering or application/membership completion. Early sourced discrepancy: readIndex.confirm releases a prefix of pending requests and retains each request ctx/from, but handleReadIndexLeaderConfirmation sends every remote response using the confirming message Hint/HintHigh, whereas local completion uses s.ctx. Followers copy the response context to ReadyToRead; pendingReadIndex.addReady selects a batch by exact SystemCtx. Thus a prefix request with a different context appears not to receive its own completion key. Timeout/GC exists and is contrary evidence against permanent resource retention; no execution or normative conclusion is claimed.

formation.explanation: Node batches proposals into Peer under raftMu. Leader stamps term/index, replicates to members and advances commitment from voting match order statistic only for its current term. Followers require preceding term match and protect the committed prefix, replying after engine persistence. Conflicts reduce next and retry; snapshots resynchronize missing history. Engine exposes committed entries to the RSM queue, whose application/session results and applied index drive client consumption. ReadIndex separately samples committed index, gathers heartbeat confirmation and releases pending prefixes to local readiness or remote responses.

context.explanation: Per-cluster term, role and applied membership define authority. Timers launch elections for eligible full members only after committed work is applied; votes require fresh log and no conflicting vote. Candidate quorum promotes and appends a current-term no-op. Higher terms demote/reset; lower terms are rejected. CheckQuorum may revoke leadership; transfer waits for target match and uses TimeoutNow, while proposals are dropped during transfer. Configuration application changes participant maps and local removal revokes leadership. Restart restores persisted term/vote/log but initializes transient follower context.

connection.explanation: Term dispatch precedes response consumption. Reset clears old votes, replication progress and pending ReadIndex support while retaining established log/commit; leader must form current-term commitment before multi-voter reads. Log freshness and committed-prefix protection constrain future leaders. Election waits for application so committed membership changes affect later quorums; RSM changes update Peer under raftMu. Old client work can be dropped or time out independently of preserved decisions. Read confirmation is transient; exact context and applied-index checks bridge its publication to requester completion, making remote prefix correlation a concrete unresolved consumption premise.

items.rationale:
Reviewed fixed artifact e4465cc7b4964f2faf0e4099ccd60176, its stored plan and harness, and raw stdout/stderr for c611aead474d4b8fa96906fb00bd1771 against claim version 1. The duty is preservation of the original SystemCtx for each remote read released by prefix confirmation, supported by the explicit per-prefix ctx/from test expectation and exact-context consumer. It is not a successful-completion deadline. Launch constructs three configured full voters and bootstrap entries. The driver applies only committed bootstrap membership and the empty leader entry; it never changes term, role, pending reads or generated message contents. Tick-driven election actually reaches term 2 and current-term commit 4; setup assertions check all nodes committed/applied at 4 and known leader 1. Storage Append/SetState precedes message exposure; Update Commit and NotifyRaftLastApplied retain caller completion order for this synchronous non-crashing history. A globally FIFO queue is a permitted restriction of per-route ordering and does not serialize the two pending reads: both are observed pending before confirmation. The two first-context heartbeats are dropped at send admission, a failure explicitly permitted by Transport.send and not retried by NodeHost.sendMessage; later traffic is generated by real Peer handlers and delivered without reordering. The known-peer Peer.Handle checks and current-term checks remain active. No background owners, sleeps, shutdown, forged replies or hidden callbacks participate.

Raw events 18 and 19 admit distinct requester identities 2 and 3, with queued=true, two pending requests, current-term commit, sampled index 4 and original contexts (1001,101)/(2001,202). Both actual nonzero-context heartbeat replies originate from voters in term 2. The first suffices with leader self-support to release the prefix. Raw result 24 for requester 2 contains one response context (2001,202), released=true, leader_pending=0 and queue_empty=true; its actual follower ReadyToRead also contains (2001,202) at index 4. Result 25 for requester 3 contains its correct (2001,202), also released=true. Thus both antecedents are observed true, not vacuous. The raw wire records independently exhibit the wrong leader-to-2 response. The monitor correlates each admitted operation by scenario/requester, not the compared context, and checks exact serialized complete High/Low context lists. Both sides use the same Go struct encoder; the observed lists each have one element, so the decisive mismatch is content identity, not cardinality or order. A comparison on response count alone would miss it. The run has no parser gaps and both admissions have results. The sent slice is an immutable copied message history accumulated by the sole goroutine; ReadyToRead values are copied before Peer.Commit clears the producer queue. Absence from pending is valid release evidence in this suffix because no reset/removal path runs and source confirm is the deletion owner.

The implementation cause agrees with the measurement: confirm retains original s.ctx and s.from while releasing the prefix, but the remote send loop uses m.Hint/m.HintHigh for each s.from; the local branch correctly uses s.ctx. The exact-key client consumer cannot associate this wrong context with requester 2 original batch. That final NodeHost timeout consequence is source-supported risk, not an executed endpoint result. No correspondence issue was found for this complete local counterexample.

Explained alternatives and bounded contrary observations: The later request succeeds in the same run: requester 3 receives its own (2001,202), so the finding is not a blanket failure of remote ReadIndex. The source local-completion branch uses s.ctx correctly; no local-prefix violation is claimed. Requester timeout/GC remains available and prevents inferring permanent resource retention. The test process passed because it emitted measurements for the monitor; process success is not the property verdict.
